chunks: And it is narrated from Salamah ibn Tammam, who said:

A man poured a pot containing broth over another man's head, and his hair went away. They disputed over that before ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he gave him a delay of one year. When his hair did not grow back, he ruled against him with the diyyah.

key_terms.بِالدِّيَةِ: with the prescribed blood money compensation
key_terms.فَأَجَّلَهُ سَنَةً: he granted a one-year delay to assess the injury
key_terms.فَذَهَبَ شَعْرُهُ: his hair fell out or was lost

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام rule when a person's hair fell out permanently after hot liquid was poured on his head?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning bodily injury that caused permanent loss of hair. He waited a year to determine whether the harm was temporary or lasting, and when the hair did not return, he ruled for the payment of full diyyah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5331 - It is narrated from Salamah ibn Tammam

that a man poured a pot of broth over another man's head, causing his hair to fall out. They disputed this matter before Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), who delayed the judgment for a year. When the man's hair did not grow back, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled that the perpetrator must pay the full blood money (diyyah).
